q: Which observation would best show that the Calvin cycle depends on light only indirectly?
options: Chloroplasts fix CO2 much faster when lit by green light than when lit by red light
Isolated thylakoids release O2 in the light even when no CO2 is present in the buffer
Rubisco extracted from leaves strongly absorbs blue light, just like chlorophyll does
Chloroplasts in the dark can fix CO2 for a short time if supplied with ATP and NADPH
explanation: When supplied with ATP and NADPH, the stroma's Calvin cycle enzymes fix CO2 without light (Arnon's experiments) – the cycle needs only the products of the light-dependent reactions, not light itself. In a living leaf, though, Rubisco and other enzymes are also activated by light-driven changes in stroma pH and Mg2+, so fixation stops quickly in darkness.
